page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the printed page number centred at the head. The left edge of the scan shows cropped fragments of the neighbouring page, which are left out. No running head, catchword or signature.

main_text.p: la, naturalis tamen intellectus capacitas non eft sublata. In statu reflectionis, divina revelatio supplet defectum incogitantiae ac ignorantiae humanae, unde ratio per actum reflexum facile potest invenire argumenta mysterium hoc demonstrantia. Hic πρῶτ[?]ων Scho-lasticorum ψευδῶς[?] in hoc negotio est, quod praesupponunt hujus similiumque Mysterio-rum cognitionem in statu confectionis & in-tegritatis fuisse non naturalem sed supernatu-ralem, quod tam divinae sapientiae ac bonita-ti, quam humanae naturae perfectioni repu-gnat, nam Status naturae perfectus debet esse instructus omnibus mediis necessariis, quibus ad summam perfectionem homo deduci possit: At summa hominis perfectio natura-lis, est summa ejus cum Deo unio, adeoque cognitio & amor. In statu defectionis & cor-ruptionis Philosophi non possunt ita facile & perfecte concludere, tamen in magis affir-mantem quam negantem partem statuere de-bent, & ex recta ratione & experientia.
VII. Demonstratio alia est a priori, alia a po-steriori; Et a priori duplex, alia quae a causis re-rum desumitur, alia quasi quae non a rebus ipsa sed menti nostrae prioribus deducitur, & haec scite

page.notes: Greek words in lines 5 and 6 of the main paragraph are uncertain in their final letters, marked [?]. The word "nostrae" at the end of the second paragraph is partly worn and read with some doubt. The long s is set as plain s throughout. The left-edge fragments belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.
